conceptZh: 牆：土、嗇，用土磚疊起來的牆。
object: a rotund cartoon chef bear in a tall hat, flinging dough with too much confidence, and a toy brick wall that has opinions
morph: the brick wall keeps dodging the chef's dough 'mortar' and wobbling away, until he outsmarts it with a rolling pin
creativeAngle: 廚師熊把麵團當水泥亂糊，牆磚一直躲開，最後用擀麵棍把磚壓回去。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean 2D/3D toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 牆 (wall), correctly formed, in a saturated solid color against a much lighter background, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with margins. Lead cast: a rotund cartoon chef bear in a tall hat, flinging dough with too much confidence, and a toy brick wall that has opinions. Warm terracotta-cream backdrop; the glyph is brick-red with lighter mortar lines. Timed beats. 0.0-1.5s: a round chef bear in a tall hat slaps a ball of dough on a counter, and a few toy bricks pop up in a row. The voice says the first 牆 as the bricks line up on the left to form the earth radical. 1.5-3.0s: he flings dough at the next brick and it hops aside; the dough lands splat on the floor. The voice says the second 牆 as bricks keep sidestepping every time he aims, one even sticking its tongue out. 3.0-4.5s: he spins his rolling pin like a staff and gently rolls the bricks back into line; they squash together and click into the finished brick-red 牆. 4.5-5.0s: the voice says 圍牆 (ㄨㄟˊ ㄑㄧㄤˊ) as a little brick fence wraps itself around the chef's feet and he hops over it. Final hold: 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is perfectly still; the chef twirls his rolling pin and a brick gives a tiny hop at the side. The glyph holds fully still and clearly readable for the last 3 seconds. Narration (off-screen, warm and unhurried, Taiwanese Mandarin, Ministry of Education readings, no erhua): the exact spoken line is 牆、牆、圍牆, syllable by syllable ㄑㄧㄤˊ、ㄑㄧㄤˊ、ㄨㄟˊ ㄑㄧㄤˊ. Two isolated utterances of the character, a short pause between them, then the word once, then silence; the voice must not add any explanation, translation or repeat. The vocabulary word is audio only. The glyph 牆 is the only text on screen: no subtitles, captions, labels, watermark, logos, clutter, flashing or strobing effects, and no real people or realistic human figures; all characters are stylized toys or cartoon animals.

conceptZh: 積木小隊疊成一座搖搖晃晃的高塔，踮著腳吱吱作響地偷偷靠近，想拿回被打瞌睡的小老鼠當枕頭的金色積木，老鼠突然睜眼，兩邊面對面尖叫，高塔向後倒下，積木嘩啦散開又一塊塊疊成磚紅色的「牆」字。
object: a squad of chunky interlocking toy bricks with little faces, stacked into one wobbly walking tower, sneaking toward a shiny gold brick that a tiny cartoon mouse is using as a pillow
morph: the tower topples backward from the face-to-face scream; the bricks fly, bounce and re-stack mid-tumble into brick-red stroke bars, left bricks standing up as the 爿 component and right bricks piling into the 嗇 component, so the crash itself builds the finished glyph 牆
creativeAngle: 前一版是安靜的壁虎爬牆，這次改成完整的「偷偷摸摸＋嚇一跳」肢體笑料：積木小隊自己就是會走路的塔，每一步都吱吱叫、每次吱叫老鼠耳朵就抖一下，把緊張感一路堆高，然後一個大尖叫讓整座塔倒下，散落的積木正好疊成磚紅色的牆字，字本身看起來就像一面積木牆，和字義直接呼應。詞語選最安全的「牆壁」，說出時畫面右下角立刻冒出一小段積木矮牆、老鼠從牆頭探頭，聽到什麼就看到什麼。
promptEn:
An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 牆 (wall), correctly formed with the component 爿 on the left and 嗇 on the right (a 來-like top over 回), built from chunky brick-red toy bricks with thin pale mortar lines, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with margins. Soft cream-yellow backdrop, warm even light, nothing busy behind.

Cast: the Brick Squad, five chunky interlocking toy bricks with tiny round eyes and stubby feet, stacked into one tall wobbly tower that walks on the bottom brick's feet; the top brick is the bossy captain who points the way. Supporting character: a tiny original cartoon mouse with huge round ears, snoring on the right side of the frame, using a shiny gold brick as a pillow.

0.0-1.5s: the brick tower peeks in from the left edge, five pairs of eyes blinking in a column. The captain points at the gold brick under the snoring mouse. The voice says the first 牆 here. The tower raises one foot in an exaggerated high tiptoe.

1.5-3.3s: the tower tiptoes across the frame left to right. Every step gives a loud comic SQUEAK, and at every squeak one of the mouse's big ears twitches while the tower freezes mid-step, leaning dangerously, bricks sweating. Three squeaky steps, each wobble bigger than the last. The captain stretches out both arms and gets its fingertips onto the gold brick.

3.3-4.3s: the mouse opens one eye. Freeze for a beat, nose to nose with the captain. Then both scream, mouths wide, the mouse's ears shooting straight up. The mouse leaps into the air and the tower rocks backward, squashes, stretches, and topples.

4.3-5.2s: BONK, the bricks hit the floor and bounce apart with cartoon squash-and-stretch, then land and stack themselves in quick clacking hops into the strokes: the left bricks stand up as 爿, the right bricks pile into 嗇, the last brick dropping into the 回 at the bottom right. The voice says the second 牆 exactly as the final brick clicks in and the whole glyph 牆 reads as one solid brick-red wall.

5.2-8.0s: the glyph 牆 holds perfectly still, centered and sharp. At about 5.5s the voice says 牆壁; at that exact moment a tiny three-row brick wall pops up in the lower right corner, well clear of the strokes, and the mouse pops its ears and grin over the top of it, holding the gold brick. The bottom brick of the squad sits dizzy at the lower left, eyes spinning in opposite directions, then gives a small proud thumbs-up. No character touches or covers the strokes.

Narration (off-screen only, warm and unhurried, Taiwanese Mandarin with Ministry of Education readings, no erhua): the exact spoken line is 牆、牆、牆壁, read syllable by syllable as ㄑㄧㄤˊ、ㄑㄧㄤˊ、ㄑㄧㄤˊ ㄅㄧˋ, with clear tones, slowly and distinctly: the character once, a short pause, the character once more, a short pause, then the word once, then silence. No extra words, no translation, no repeat. Sound effects are soft toy squeaks and clacks, quieter than the voice, no startling loud noises. The glyph 牆 is the only text on screen: no subtitles, captions, labels, watermark or logos, no flashing or strobing, no real people or realistic human figures, all characters are stylized toys and cartoon animals, bright but not neon, no white blowouts.
